title: Vehicle Overheats With A/C On
summary: Cooling and A/C load workflow for overheating that appears when condenser heat and fan demand increase.
intro: Overheating with A/C on usually means the cooling system is struggling with added condenser heat, fan demand, airflow restriction, or low coolant reserve.
common_sounds: Temperature climbs with A/C on at idle
Cooling fan runs loudly, intermittently, or not at all
Coolant smell or overflow after idling with A/C
quick_checks: Verify coolant level and pressure-test if loss is suspected
Confirm cooling fan command and airflow with A/C requested
Inspect condenser and radiator fins for debris or blockage
Compare temperature at idle with A/C on versus off
Check thermostat and circulation if overheating continues while driving
inspection_priority: Check coolant level and leak evidence first
Verify fan operation with A/C request
Inspect condenser/radiator airflow before replacing cooling parts
confidence_cues: Pressure test if coolant loss exists
common_causes: Cooling fan not moving enough air
Thermostat, radiator, or water pump weakness under load

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Fan and Airflow Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when overheating is strongest at idle with A/C requested.
checks: Inspect relays, fuses, wiring, and fan motor response
Clean debris between condenser and radiator

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Coolant Reserve Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use when the system overheats with load or shows coolant smell, loss, or poor circulation.
checks: Inspect radiator, hoses, cap, thermostat, and water pump clues
Bleed air after any coolant service

recommended_repairs.title: Cooling Fan Diagnosis
recommended_repairs.description: Use when overheating changes with A/C request or idle airflow.

recommended_repairs.title: Coolant Pressure Test
recommended_repairs.description: Use when coolant smell, loss, or overflow is present.

recommended_repairs.title: Radiator Blueprint
recommended_repairs.description: Related when airflow through the radiator stack or heat rejection is weak.
